extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature — scientists, engineers, geologists, chemists, patent practitioners, and academic book reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and expectations used by reviewers to judge scientific and technical books (clarity, scope, accuracy, appendices, methodology, and practical utility). Covers textbooks, technical primers, regional geological surveys, and professional works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical sequencing of subject matter (practice → validity → rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: “After a brief introductory survey, they first deal with the manner of obtaining a patent, detailing the procedure in the Patent Office and in possible opposition proceedings. Their next concern is the establishment in the courts of the validity of the patent ... Finally, the privileges and responsibilities associated with the possession of a valid patent are discussed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting material in an order that links practical procedure, legal validation, and then rights/responsibilities makes underlying principles easy to follow and aids comprehension for both legal and non-legal readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and conciseness; avoid undue technicality
rubrics_metrics.description: “the treatment throughout is clear and concise and avoids undue stress upon legal technicalities, the book should commend itself not only to legal practitioners but also to business men, directors of industrial research, and others who are interested in the protection and commercial exploitation of inventions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for clear, concise exposition tailored to intended audiences; where possible reduce heavy technical/legal jargon so the work is accessible to practitioners and non-specialists involved in application or commercialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix value: include consolidated statutes and leading cases; omit needless reprints
rubrics_metrics.description: “An appendix, which extends to a little over half the book, contains as its most valuable features the Patents and Designs Acts in a consolidated form, and a list of the leading cases ... Of lesser value relatively are the reprints of the patents forms, the Patents Rules, and the war legislation ... these reprints ... might very reasonably have been dispensed with as adding unnecessarily to the cost of a very useful book.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices should prioritise consolidated legislation and curated lists of leading cases or essential reference material; avoid reprinting voluminous standard forms/rules that add cost but little value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucid description and mapping of regional geological structure; emphasise major discoveries and economic relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: “In this memoir the structure of the district is lucidly described. The most remarkable feature is the great Sugarbush fault ... This is a new discovery of great importance.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear text descriptions supported by maps and surveys; highlight newly discovered structural features, their inferred chronology, and their economic implications (e.g., relation to reefs/mineralization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic economic and feasibility assessment of technical proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentary on alternative power schemes: sunlight plants competing with coal at specified prices; waves not economical; tides promising where structural work is not too costly; “The estimated costs of the Severn Scheme the author thinks too low.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or proposing technical schemes, include credible cost estimates, comparisons with alternatives, and careful consideration of structural and regional feasibility rather than optimistic or unsupported figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate level of treatment and concision for the intended audience; avoid rambling and irrelevant discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: “The author has wasted a good deal of the space at his disposal by a rambling style and by irrelevant discussions. ... Much of the text deals with very elementary matters, which should be assumed to be known by the readers. In consequence, the remaining space is insufficient to render possible a clear description, in sufficient detail, of apparatus for technical filtration.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match depth to the stated audience: omit elementary material that wastes space for technical readers and use saved space to supply necessary detailed descriptions (e.g., apparatus and methods) for practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness: include essential modern topics and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique noting omissions: “Specific heats at low temperatures might have been mentioned, and we also miss any allusion to Werner’s theory and the cyanide process for silver extraction.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks and technical primers should cover current, relevant theories and industrially important processes; omission of such items weakens utility as an introductory or reference work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and precision of definitions, factual statements and reported data
rubrics_metrics.description: “The definitions in connexion with the phase rule (§ 45) are not sufficiently precise. Stas’s silver was not so pure as is implied (§ 281); the existence of MnO2 is doubtful; stannous oxide is olive coloured, not black; and the atomic weight of nitrogen is not a whole number within the limits of experimental error (§ 508).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure precise definitions, correct chemical/physical facts, accurate statements about experimental purity and measured quantities, and correct descriptions of material properties; avoid misleading or incorrect assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility through appendices and bibliographies
rubrics_metrics.description: “It gives in a very comprehensive form a quantity of useful information, legal and medical, concerning the mentally defective child. ... The appendices supply a list of institutions ... the medical certificate forms under the Mental Deficiency Act, and a list of the Binet-Simon tests. There is also an excellent bibliography.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include practical reference material (institution lists, standard forms, test inventories) and a strong bibliography to increase a book’s value to practitioners and administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of mathematical/theoretical treatment and practical applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor’s plan: “It has been part of my plan to separate the mathematical treatment of a subject and its practical applications. In this manner I hoped to increase the utility of the work to various classes of readers, some of whom are interested chiefly in the theory, while others are more closely concerned with the more practical details.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider structuring works so that rigorous theory and practical application are distinct (separate chapters/volumes) to better serve readers with different needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include elastic-strain analysis and both quantitative and qualitative interpretations in studies of tool action
rubrics_metrics.description: “So far as the tool itself is concerned, it is only useful so long as it does not become permanently deformed, and to the maker of tool steel, the stresses and strains produced within the elastic range are therefore matters of interest ... In another section an account is given of the stress effects in the work when the tool is removing material therefrom, which are quantitative within the range for which the laws of photo-elasticity are known, and qualitative in the plastic region ... They show, for example, that the action is sometimes discontinuous, and under other conditions is not so.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports on cutting/tool action should analyse stresses in the tool (elastic range), provide quantitative photo-elastic data where applicable, interpret plastic-region effects qualitatively, and discuss observed phenomena (e.g., discontinuous action, curling behavior) across speed regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous observational protocol, instrument control, and replication before inferring geophysical change
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of gravity observations: differences attributable to stand support conditions, possible molecular change in pendulum materials, wearing of agate edges; recommendation to re-observe Peninsular stations (Colaba, Mysore, Jubbulpore) to check for real changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting apparent changes in geophysical quantities, control for experimental set-up (support, temperature, stand), instrument wear/calibration, and perform independent re-observations at multiple reference stations before concluding a real geophysical change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical precision in definitions and derivations; avoid over-generalised statements about extremal properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Response to claims about world-line lengths not being minima; cautions that methods of deriving geodesic equations must be used carefully and checked (e.g., statements about minima/maxima may reflect the method rather than Einstein's equations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in mathematical definitions (geodesic, extremal), employ coordinate-independent formulations, use multiple derivation methods where possible, and verify functional conditions (e.g., linearity conditions) before asserting general extremal properties.
